correctness.rationale: For every finite poset the K_x argument derives all nuclei uniquely from subsets. Direct composite tests distinguish bottom points belonging to neither, one or both supports, yielding exactly the two inclusion conditions. Three disjoint lower-support cases provide the polynomial. The image rank is the number of upper sets of the intersection support. The proof is unrestricted for m,n>=2; the stdlib checker exhaustively verifies finite examples and direct independent nucleus generation in four smallest cases.

value.rationale: The two-antichain height-two family is the first natural non-chain test for incompatibility of nuclei. The theorem supplies a complete weighted compatibility census and every composite image rank, plus nonisomorphic level-exchanged algebras sharing the entire spectrum. General nuclear-range theory and small-value computation alone do not provide these structural invariants.
